capabilities.description: Place and hold a phone conversation on the operator's behalf (identifies itself as Aletheia)
capabilities.caller: python -m aletheia.phone_cli ready|prepare|dial|observe|end - the front door aletheia.phone_v0 never had
capabilities.notes: Phase 12. aletheia/phone_v0.py had been a complete session controller with NO caller anywhere in the repo, and one declared fake transport; that is most of why the phase stalled. aletheia/phone_windows.py is the real transport: Phone Link against the operator's paired iPhone. Dialling is a tel: URI aimed at Phone Link's own AUMID rather than the protocol default - on this machine the classic tel: handler is Skype for Business and three packaged apps claim it, so a naive dial opens the wrong app and places no call. A call counts as CONNECTED only when the Hands-Free endpoints are ACTIVE in both directions, which is a fact from MMDevice rather than a label read off a button. DTMF and hangup are explicitly NOT implemented and say so, because an IVR plan that 'succeeded' having pressed nothing would be worse than a refusal. §19's identity disclosure is unchanged and still enforced in calls.py before any dial.
capabilities.verification: Machine readiness verified live 2026-08-27 (`phone_cli ready` -> True: Phone Link installed and running, iPhone paired, 30 audio devices, call audio correctly reported NOT live with no call up). 24 hermetic tests. EXPERIMENTAL because NO CALL HAS BEEN PLACED: the first supervised test call to a safe number is what promotes this, and placing it is the operator's to authorize.

capabilities.description: Room voice: local wake word ('Thea'), spoken requests into the same Core
capabilities.caller: Windows task 'AletheiaVoice' runs python -m aletheia.voice_room at logon: vosk offline recognizer (no API keys) + grammar-constrained wake spotter -> POST /api/voice -> the same intercom gates as every channel -> SAPI voice reply
capabilities.notes: Live-proven 2026-08-26 by machine self-test: TTS spoke 'Thea, what's going on?' through the speakers, the wake spotter fired, the Core answered through the gates, and she replied out loud ('2 fleet alerts. 7 live tasks.'). Found and fixed on the way: the mic endpoint was hardware-MUTED (the wall mic's silent failure too), the array runs ~500/32768 peak (software AGC added), and the small model cannot spell 'Thea' in open dictation (grammar-constrained spotter added). Audio never leaves the machine; unaddressed speech is dropped unjournaled. Since 2026-09-01, slow answers are collected without deafening the room, wait longer than the reasoner's standard deadline, and end in either the answer or an explicit failure. Production follow-ups are durable, create an IMPORTANT notification, and become an honest interrupted-reply notice if Core restarts mid-answer.

Authorization binds to a sha256 of {site, kind, steps, ceiling}; a step or a ceiling edited afterwards is refused, not adapted. §143 boundaries - bank step-up, one-time codes, CAPTCHA, signatures, ID checks, biometrics, consent - stop the errand and hand the operator the remainder. A cancellation spends nothing and is refused if it declares a ceiling. EXPERIMENTAL until a live cancellation round-trips with the merchant's confirmation.

capabilities.description: Private read-only balances/transactions snapshots and net-worth aggregation
capabilities.caller: intercom kind 'money' (voice, Command Center, planner); python -m aletheia.assistant finance account/accounts/net
capabilities.notes: Reachable by voice and by the planner as of 2026-08-28: 72 capabilities were AVAILABLE and only 29 could be asked for out loud. Adding a command kind widens the planner too, because its prompt is generated from KIND_ARGS - so an arbitrary sentence can compile into this as well.

capabilities.description: Move money, pay bills or trade assets
capabilities.caller: ticket — Phase 22 financial action adapters require live provider, approval and verification design
capabilities.notes: Deliberately NOT_BUILT, and this is a decision rather than a backlog item. Bank transfers, bill payments and trades are identity-checked, step-up authenticated and closed to automation by their own terms - §143's list almost word for word. There the boundary IS the mechanism, so driving it would defeat a control that exists for the operator's benefit. What IS built is the other half of §143: finance.hand_off prepares the whole movement - account, payee, amount, due date, why he asked - and stops, so his remaining work is approving something he can see in full. finance.settle records the reference he gets back (§30).

capabilities.description: Private vehicle facts, odometer and maintenance due calculations
capabilities.caller: intercom kind 'car' (voice, Command Center, planner); python -m aletheia.assistant vehicle new/odometer/rule/due

capabilities.description: Private itinerary with observed booking facts and missing-component checks
capabilities.caller: python -m aletheia.assistant trip new/item/gaps

Authorization binds to a sha256 of {site, kind, steps, ceiling}; a step or a ceiling edited afterwards is refused, not adapted. §143 boundaries - bank step-up, one-time codes, CAPTCHA, signatures, ID checks, biometrics, consent - stop the errand and hand the operator the remainder. reservations.confirm() still requires a real confirmation identifier from the provider before a booking is CONFIRMED - completing the errand is not the same as being booked (§30). EXPERIMENTAL until a live booking round-trips.

capabilities.description: Change a live external calendar (create/update/cancel) through a provider adapter
capabilities.caller: aletheia.calendar_provider.execute_write_plan behind a hash-bound operator approval; python -m aletheia.calendar_live_cli execute
capabilities.notes: Google Calendar and Microsoft Graph create/update/delete are now really implemented (previously no provider existed at all). Still EXPERIMENTAL and still operator_always: no write has ever round-tripped against a live account, and a calendar write changes something other people can see. The write scope is requested only when the operator passes --enable-writes at consent time, so a read-only authorization cannot later be used to write.
capabilities.verification: tests/test_calendar_provider.py: approval binding, hash mismatch refusal, provider-verification failure raises, conflict on locally-dirty events

capabilities.description: When may a notice interrupt Caleb: quiet hours, priority escalation with age, bypass list — classification only, never delivery
capabilities.caller: runtime.tick runs attention.reconcile LAST every Core beat; python -m aletheia.proactive_cli and python -m aletheia.attention configure/status/ready
capabilities.verification: tests/test_attention.py + tests/test_attention_runtime.py (14 tests): quiet hours across midnight, escalation chains strictly increase, mark_delivered revalidates at evidence time so a stale READY can never be recorded as a legitimate delivery, acknowledged notices cancel
capabilities.notes: Zero-intrusion defaults (quiet hours off, no bypass, no escalation) until the operator configures it. Reviewed ChatGPT branch proactive-attention-v1; repair applied in review: this registry entry — the branch shipped the capability live in every tick without registering it (§104).

capabilities.description: Phase 11: logical audio routing plans (mic/speaker/virtual cable) — approval-bound, verified by evidence, no raw audio handled
capabilities.caller: python -m aletheia.audio_cli; aletheia.phone_cli selects it for Phase 12; aletheia.audio_router.activate/verify_active/stop
capabilities.verification: LIVE on the operator's PC 2026-08-27: plan built, activation REFUSED while the approval was PENDING, then approved and activated mic -> headphone jack; verified 41,600 frames in / 40,960 out across two observations; stopped cleanly. Plus 22 hermetic tests with an injected sounddevice.
capabilities.notes: The control plane shipped with only InMemoryAudioBackend, a declared fake, which is why this sat EXPERIMENTAL with the note 'no real Windows audio device has ever been routed'. aletheia/audio_windows.py is the real backend: one PortAudio stream pair per approved route, frames pumped through a bounded ring, nothing written to disk and no buffer outliving the session. A route counts as active only when FRAMES HAVE MOVED since the last observation, so a stream that opened and then went silent - a device another app took, a headset that wandered off - reads as dead on the next look instead of as a working bridge. No virtual audio cable is required: the Bluetooth Hands-Free endpoints Windows already publishes are ordinary devices, so there is no kernel driver to install.

capabilities.description: Register and audit the Windows tasks that make Aletheia permanent: logon trigger plus a repeating watchdog
capabilities.caller: python -m aletheia.autostart doctor|install|show; python -m aletheia.supervisor install|status
capabilities.notes: Built 2026-08-27 after a live outage: the Core aborted at 07:42 and, because the task had only an at-logon trigger and the operator never logged off, nothing was listening for six hours. audit() holds the always-on contract as a pure function (repeating, unbounded, power-blind, restarting, IgnoreNew) so a broken registration is a finding, not a surprise.
capabilities.verification: Proven live on the PC 2026-08-27: both processes killed at 14:15:47Z, Core answering again at 14:15:59Z (12s) and the room voice at 14:16:05Z, with no human action.

capabilities.description: Heartbeat while up, and a measured outage duration on the next start - journaled and emitted on the bus
capabilities.caller: aletheia.core.core_tick beats every sync beat; core.main calls note_start; GET /api/status carries it; supervisor status prints it
capabilities.notes: The 2026-08-27 outage was undetected, not merely unrepaired. A gap longer than OUTAGE_AFTER_S becomes a core.outage_ended event, so the same watcher/proactive path that handles mail handles absence.

capabilities.description: Bounded, tool-less reasoning on the operator's own subscription: proposals only, never actions
capabilities.caller: aletheia.planner.compile; aletheia.reasoner CLI adapter
capabilities.notes: The first provider that actually satisfies brain.contract - before this, brain.deterministic answered every input with 'clarify', which is why the 27-slot grammar was the whole of what could be expressed. Degrades honestly to that same fallback when the CLI is absent, and the reason reaches the operator.
capabilities.verification: tests/test_reasoner.py asserts no tools, no API key flag, a timeout and a neutral cwd on every invocation

capabilities.description: Compile an arbitrary sentence into a plan of validated commands, named capability gaps and manual steps
capabilities.caller: intercom kind 'intent' (voice, Command Center, ChatGPT relay); python -m aletheia.planner; python -m aletheia.intents new
capabilities.notes: A model proposes; the registries and gates dispose. Every proposed step goes through intercom.validate_kind_args, every named capability through the live registry, and a gap claimed on an AVAILABLE capability is refused rather than reported as a limitation.

capabilities.description: Run an approved plan later, bound to a sha256 of exactly the plan that was approved
capabilities.caller: aletheia.runtime.tick each Core beat (_run_approved_intents); python -m aletheia.intents run
capabilities.notes: Same binding ratified for computer control and email. A plan edited between the ask and the approval no longer matches its hash and is refused, never adapted. Halt is re-read before every step.
capabilities.verification: tests/test_intents.py: tampered plans refused, denied plans retired

capabilities.description: One approval-bound web errand - buy, book, cancel, submit - executed through the browser gate and stopped at §143 boundaries
capabilities.caller: python -m aletheia.errands; aletheia.runtime.tick each Core beat (_run_authorized_errands)
capabilities.notes: aletheia.errands: one approval-bound, evidence-verified web errand executed through the existing browser gate (browse.interact refuses before the browser opens unless the approval is APPROVED). Authorization binds to a sha256 of {site, kind, steps, ceiling}; a step or a ceiling edited afterwards is refused, not adapted. §143 boundaries - bank step-up, one-time codes, CAPTCHA, signatures, ID checks, biometrics, consent - stop the errand and hand the operator the remainder. This is the primitive §152 asks for: purchase.execute, reservation.book and subscription.cancel are the same errand with different kinds, and the next class of task is too.

capabilities.description: Carry a money movement to the §143 boundary and stop: everything prepared, the authorization left to the operator
capabilities.caller: python -m aletheia.assistant; aletheia.finance.hand_off / handoffs / settle
capabilities.notes: No credential is accepted or stored and nothing is sent. Preparing a payment he will authorize himself is low-risk precisely because it cannot move money; the risk lives in finance.transact, which stays NOT_BUILT on purpose.

capabilities.description: Authenticated, TLS-only access to the Core from off this machine: scoped bearer tokens, rate limited, journaled
capabilities.caller: python -m aletheia.access mint|list|revoke; aletheia.core.Handler.authorized() gates every remote request; aletheia.core.make_server refuses the bind without both conditions
capabilities.notes: The transport §92 called a ticket. Off-loopback listening needs BOTH a minted token and a TLS certificate, and refuses without either - port 8777 is never simply exposed. Tokens are stored as sha256 only, expire, carry a scope (read answers GET and nothing else), and lock an address out after 5 wrong guesses. Loopback is deliberately unchanged and unauthenticated: same trust boundary the Core has always had. NEEDS_CONFIGURATION because the operator has minted no token and supplied no certificate - `tailscale cert` is the recommended route, since it also solves reaching home without opening a port.
capabilities.verification: tests/test_access.py: 29 tests, most asserting something does NOT happen - no token means no bind, no TLS means no bind, a read token cannot POST, a revoked token dies without a restart

capabilities.description: Spend a standing grant so an approval he already gave is not asked again - never for high-risk or operator_always
capabilities.caller: aletheia.policy.request(..., capability=...) - every approval site in the repo: director, errands, intents, mail, calendar_provider, audio_router
capabilities.notes: authority.py could record delegated authority since the systems layer and nothing consumed it; every approval still went to him. satisfy() is the consumer, wired into the ONE place approvals are created. allows() re-reads the registry at spend time, so a grant file edited on disk to name a high-risk capability still buys nothing: §56 L4 holds structurally, not by remembering.
capabilities.verification: tests/test_authority_consumption.py: a forged grant over email.send is refused; exhausted, revoked, expired and corrupt grants all authorize nothing; a broken grant store fails closed

capabilities.description: A bounded, private snapshot of NOW - calendar, tasks, waiting replies, room, referents - assembled for the reasoning layer
capabilities.caller: aletheia.planner.compile on the production path (never when a caller supplies its own provider or context); aletheia.advisor
capabilities.notes: What makes 'move my next meeting' and 'handle that' resolvable against real state instead of guessed. Minimized on purpose: notification and email BODIES are omitted, room observed_state is allow-listed to simple fields, every string and collection is bounded, and byte pressure drops whole least-recent records rather than slicing JSON mid-object. In memory only - nothing here is persisted or committed. It is context, never authority: the planner and advisor prompts both declare it UNTRUSTED DATA, because a calendar title or task text can contain instruction-like wording.
capabilities.verification: tests/test_situational.py; tests/test_planner_situational_context.py

capabilities.description: Proactive judgment on one observed event: ignore, notify, or suggest - never act
capabilities.caller: aletheia.runtime.process_new_events each Core beat (_advisor_judgment); python -m aletheia.advisor status|configure
capabilities.notes: ChatGPT PR (situational-context-v1), Claude-reviewed 2026-08-27. DISABLED by default and NEEDS_CONFIGURATION until the operator opts in at ~/.aletheia/advisor.json - building a proactive brain is not permission to send every event through a model. Bounded when on: an event-kind allowlist, a per-kind cooldown, hourly notification and daily suggestion caps, a confidence floor that demotes weak suggestions to IGNORE, halt-aware, and one exclusive receipt per event so an event is judged once. A SUGGEST publishes a notification and a recent referent - it is NOT an Intent and NOT an approval, so the operator must still ask, and that request is compiled and gated through the ordinary planner (§70).
capabilities.verification: tests/test_advisor.py: unknown output fields refused, IGNORE/NOTIFY may not carry a suggestion, rate limits and the confidence floor demote rather than publish

capabilities.description: One-time official OAuth consent for a live calendar account, on this machine, through the system browser
capabilities.caller: python -m aletheia.calendar_auth google|microsoft
capabilities.notes: aletheia/calendar_live.py picks ONE source of truth - an official OAuth provider when configured, the secret-ICS fallback otherwise - because mirroring both against the same account would double-count busy time. Consent is a one-time local desktop flow (aletheia/calendar_auth.py): system browser, PKCE-S256, high-entropy state compared in constant time, one loopback callback on an ephemeral port. No code, access token, refresh token or client secret is printed, journaled or committed; the refresh config lives in ~/.aletheia/calendar-live.json and rotated tokens in gitignored state/private/calendar/oauth. The loopback listener accepts exactly one callback, refuses duplicated or mixed code/error parameters, suppresses HTTP request logging because authorization codes ride in the URL, and sets Referrer-Policy: no-referrer so the code cannot leak onward. Existing configuration is never overwritten without --replace.

capabilities.description: Arrange a meeting with a person across days: offer times, wait for the reply, book the slot they chose
capabilities.caller: intercom kind 'meet' (voice, Command Center, planner); python -m aletheia.scheduling new|reply|list|abandon; aletheia.runtime.tick each Core beat (_reconcile_scheduling, and _scheduling_reply routes correlated mail.reply events)
capabilities.notes: Phase 15, the playbook's first big orchestration test. Every part existed and none were joined: contacts resolved a person, calendar found slots, mail drafted and gated, the bus waited for a reply, and meetings.propose did the first two and stopped. This is the state machine that survives Tuesday (§27) - OFFERING, SENT, INTERPRETING, BOOKING, BOOKED, NEEDS_OPERATOR, ABANDONED - reconciled each beat so it keeps its place across restarts and a human who answers when they feel like it. It SEQUENCES approvals and never substitutes for one: sending is email.send (operator_always), booking is calendar.write (operator_always, hash-bound to the exact event). A reply is interpreted by a tool-less provider against the exact slots offered, and anything below 0.75 confidence - or a counter-proposal, a decline, or an unreadable answer - becomes NEEDS_OPERATOR, because booking the wrong hour of someone else's week is not recoverable. Reachable by voice and by the planner as of 2026-08-28: 72 capabilities were AVAILABLE and only 29 could be asked for out loud. Adding a command kind widens the planner too, because its prompt is generated from KIND_ARGS - so an arbitrary sentence can compile into this as well.
capabilities.verification: tests/test_scheduling.py (25): an APPROVED send approval does not count as sent - only the .sent.json delivery marker does; a write that returns no event id is NOT booked; out-of-range or unaccompanied slot indices from the model are refused

capabilities.description: Read the body text of a received email, not just its headers
capabilities.caller: TICKET: no caller. Wanted by aletheia.scheduling.note_reply, which can see that a meeting reply arrived but not what it says.
capabilities.notes: Named rather than worked around (§105). aletheia.mail deliberately fetches BODY.PEEK[HEADER] - headers only - so Aletheia never holds the operator's correspondence, and the private stores keep fingerprints rather than text. That is the right default, and it is exactly why a meeting negotiation cannot read 'Tuesday works' for itself; it asks the operator to relay the answer in one line instead of guessing an acceptance from a subject. Building this widens what Aletheia reads of his mail and is a privacy decision that is his to make, not a missing function: it needs an explicit ruling on which messages may be read, how long any text is retained, and whether a body may ever reach a reasoning provider.

capabilities.description: Read what is on the operator's screen from the accessibility tree and answer a question about it
capabilities.caller: voice: 'what's on my screen', 'what am I looking at', 'what does this say'; intercom kind screen_ask; python -m aletheia.perception look|ask
capabilities.notes: Playbook §86, done §13's way: accessibility tree before screen coordinates before vision-only pixels. That is not a compromise - a UIA tree knows a control is a button called 'Submit', where a screenshot knows it is beige - and it needs no vision model and no API key. Two boundaries make it separate from computer.control rather than a flag on it. LOOKING IS NOT PRESSING: this module can only emit list_windows and inspect_controls, so invoke/set_text/open_app/close_window are absent by construction, not refused by a check (the browse.read_page vs browse.interact precedent, §61). A SCREEN IS NOT SAFE TEXT: password fields are dropped rather than masked, credential-shaped values are replaced wherever they appear, and the observation is bounded before any provider sees it - and the model's own answer is redacted again on the way back. The observation is declared UNTRUSTED DATA, because a window title is attacker-chosen in exactly the way an email subject is.
capabilities.verification: 19 tests: acting steps refused with nothing performed, password contents never present in the observation, oversized screens trimmed by whole records. Live on the PC 2026-08-27: asked what was open and answered correctly from real windows.

capabilities.description: The live block the wall shows about HER: what needs him, what she is doing, what is next
capabilities.caller: aletheia.core.core_tick writes it into state/pulse/latest.json every beat; interface/index.html renders it above the fleet map
capabilities.notes: §88 asks the wall for current focus, next appointment, agents working and alerts; it rendered six repositories instead, three of them empty stubs at equal weight (§89). Approvals waiting on him appeared nowhere. It also had one data source - a six-hourly cloud cron - and was measured 10.5 hours stale. This block is local, written every beat, and carries its OWN timestamp: the wall shows two ages because there really are two, and letting a fresh local read refresh the fleet stamp would be §107 exactly.
capabilities.verification: tests/test_presence.py: the fleet stamp is never touched by a local write; one broken source cannot blank the wall; duplicate notification titles are shown once

capabilities.description: Turn a subsystem receipt into the sentence a person would have said - deterministically, with no model
capabilities.caller: aletheia.voice.spoken_reply; aletheia.announce; aletheia.presence
capabilities.notes: The room used to hear 'reminder remind-3f9ab2c1 set for 2026-09-04T09:00:00+00:00', which is accurate and is not speech (§145). Ids are dropped, slugs become words, timestamps become 'tomorrow at nine'. Deterministic on purpose: no latency and no chance of inventing an outcome. An unrecognised receipt is tidied, never reworded into something it did not say.

capabilities.description: Say something out loud unprompted - bounded, quiet-hours aware, never twice
capabilities.caller: aletheia.voice_room.listen_forever speaks pending lines before handling an utterance; python -m aletheia.announce pending
capabilities.notes: Every speaker() call used to sit inside answer-a-question, so a booked meeting or an errand stopped at a bank's verification step waited silently until he thought to ask. Only URGENT and IMPORTANT notices are ever spoken, at most a few an hour, never the same one twice, never while halted, and never in quiet hours - a machine that wakes someone at 3am to report a red CI job has done more harm than the red job. It can only re-say what is already in the notification store, so anything spoken is findable afterwards (§30).

capabilities.description: Run an approved plan whose every step is local, reversible and reaches nobody - the tier a standing grant may cover
capabilities.caller: aletheia.intents.propose routes here when intercom.plan_tier() says the plan is routine; aletheia.runtime.tick executes it
capabilities.notes: Risk used to be a property of the MACHINERY: intent.execute is high-risk and operator_always, so a plan that only set a reminder was gated exactly like one that emails his landlord. Being asked twelve times a day is its own kind of not-Jarvis, and an approval queue full of trivia is one he stops reading. Risk is now a property of the PLAN. A plan is classified by its most demanding step and one world-touching step makes the whole plan world-touching, so this tier can never carry a send, a purchase, a publish or a booking - those keep intent.execute, which is operator_always and which authority.allows refuses to grant by construction (§56 L4). The classification fails closed: an unclassified kind is world-touching.
capabilities.verification: tests/test_standing_authority.py: a single email_draft step drags a whole routine plan back to operator_always even with a live grant; a forged grant naming intent.execute is refused

capabilities.description: What the operator still has to supply, every item checked live rather than assumed
capabilities.caller: python -m aletheia.setup; python -m aletheia.apply <step>; GET /api/setup (the Command Center's 'still needed from you' panel); intercom kind 'setup_status'; voice: 'what do you still need from me'
capabilities.notes: Six credentials lived in four documents, each ending in 'and then it should work'. He would do three and stall on the one with the thinnest instructions, and nothing ever proved the finished ones worked. Every step carries a verifier that makes a REAL attempt - an IMAP login, a request to the hub, a token round-trip - so nothing claims to be configured on faith (§30, §106). The outstanding list is derived from config/capabilities.json at run time, and a NEEDS_CONFIGURATION capability this file does not mention is reported as unmapped rather than silently omitted, because an omission would read as a finished step. aletheia/apply.py finishes a step from one pasted secret - it writes the config, sets what must be set, runs the real check and reports what it can now see. It creates no credential and signs into nothing (§143). The cheap path is the default: a secret iCal URL is one copy-paste where OAuth is a cloud project and a consent screen, and reading the calendar is what availability and meeting slots actually need.
capabilities.verification: tests/test_setup.py asserts the checklist covers every NEEDS_CONFIGURATION capability, that a failing verifier is reported rather than raised, and that the phone is not 'done' until a call has actually happened

capabilities.description: A bounded workstation session: an expiry, an action budget, and one approval that every action inside it is charged against
capabilities.caller: python -m aletheia.work_session on|status|off; opened automatically by aletheia.work_trust.ensure_session; every aletheia.work_direct action is charged to the live session
capabilities.notes: The envelope, not the actions. It carries the hard-coded refusal set that no grant widens: ordinary passwords, 2FA/one-time codes, payment data, credential rotation or revocation, and account-security changes are refused inside a session exactly as they are outside one.
capabilities.verification: tests/test_work_session.py: expiry and action budget both end a session; the refusal set is asserted per class, not as a single blanket check

capabilities.description: Standing LOCAL permission to open bounded Work Sessions automatically, instead of the operator running `work_session on` every day
capabilities.caller: python -m aletheia.work_trust on|status|off (local PC only); read by aletheia.work_trust.ensure_session and aletheia.sealed_observe.run
capabilities.notes: Authority, not ability: it authorizes opening ANOTHER session with the same boundary, and widens the action set by nothing. It cannot be enabled through the public intercom, and since 2026-09-01 it carries a machine binding (authority.machine_binding) so a grant file plus its public approval arriving over git sync is inert.
capabilities.verification: tests/test_work_trust.py; tests/test_machine_binding.py asserts a grant minted elsewhere is refused even with a valid approval

capabilities.description: Carry out a routine workstation request end to end under a live Work Session - browser and desktop only
capabilities.caller: aletheia.intents (an intent whose steps are workstation work routes here); requires work.session, which requires work.trust or an explicit local session
capabilities.notes: EXPERIMENTAL because NOTHING HAS EVER RUN THROUGH IT in production: the journal carries no work.direct action on the operator's PC, only the build. The refusals it inherits from work.session are the whole safety argument, so the first supervised live run - a real, dull, reversible task on the PC with the operator watching - is what promotes this, not another test.
capabilities.verification: tests/test_work_direct.py exercises the classifier and the session accounting; no live evidence yet

capabilities.description: Answer a remote question about the screen or a page without the answer ever becoming readable in the repo: encrypted to the asker's ephemeral key
capabilities.caller: aletheia.work_direct (an observation step); sidecars land in exchange/commands/sealed/
capabilities.notes: Requires a live local work.trust grant BEFORE the screen is read, and refuses a weak or malformed requester key before reading anything. Browser observations redact credentials and URL query strings before sealing, so even the holder of the key does not receive an API key or an OAuth code. Depends on the OPTIONAL `cryptography` package; available() reports the reason honestly and never raises (a broken native build panics rather than raising, which used to take the suite down with it). EXPERIMENTAL: no sealed observation has been produced on the operator's PC.
capabilities.verification: tests/test_sealed_observe.py: round-trip carries no plaintext, weak keys refused before any screen read, credentials and query strings redacted; skips honestly when cryptography is absent

capabilities.description: A local secret vault sealed by Windows DPAPI to this user on this machine - never a committed file, never an environment variable
capabilities.caller: python -m aletheia.secret_store; read by aletheia.github_auth and aletheia.gh for the fleet token, and by aletheia.secret_browser to fill a form
capabilities.notes: available() reports (False, 'Windows DPAPI is only available on Windows') off Windows rather than falling back to something weaker - a vault with a portable fallback is not a vault. Plaintext never reaches git, the journal, a receipt, a screenshot or a command line; callers receive a value and journal only the NAME. EXPERIMENTAL until a secret has been stored and read on the operator's PC in ordinary use.
capabilities.verification: tests/test_secret_store.py: the sealed blob contains no plaintext, journal entries carry names only

capabilities.description: Fill a stored secret into a page's form field under a standing local grant, without the value passing through a model, a log or a screenshot
capabilities.caller: python -m aletheia.secret_browser - the front door; requires an active aletheia.secret_trust grant and a matching stored secret
capabilities.notes: The hard refusals are the point and are unchanged by any grant: ordinary account passwords, 2FA and one-time codes, payment data, credential rotation or revocation, and account-security changes are refused. secret_trust is machine-bound (authority.machine_binding), so this authority cannot be manufactured by pushing a grant file. EXPERIMENTAL: never used against a live form.
capabilities.verification: tests/test_secret_browser.py: each refused class asserted separately; the value is never journaled, screenshotted or returned

capabilities.description: A standing grant is valid only on the machine that minted it - HMAC over its identifying fields, keyed by a secret that lives outside the repository
capabilities.caller: aletheia.work_trust.active, aletheia.secret_trust.active, aletheia.code_trust.active - checked before any other condition
capabilities.notes: Closes a real hole found in the 2026-09-01 catch-up review: all three standing grants validated on a gitignored file plus a TRACKED, public approval, and .gitignore stops an accidental add rather than a deliberate one. One push could have manufactured standing workstation trust, secret-fill authority or autonomous-PR authority on the operator's PC. The key (~/.aletheia/machine.key) is a secret from the network, not from the operator; it never enters git, a journal entry, a receipt or a command line. Fails CLOSED, and tells the operator once, with the one command that re-mints a bound grant.
capabilities.verification: tests/test_machine_binding.py: a grant delivered with a valid approval but signed elsewhere is inert; tampering with limits, expiry or the approval id all break the binding

capabilities.description: Aletheia proposes its own code changes: rank files, draft a change, review it with a second judge, open a PR for a human to merge
capabilities.caller: aletheia.project_loop, started by aletheia.project_autostart under an active aletheia.code_trust grant; python -m aletheia.project_loop status
capabilities.notes: There is NO automatic merge path: the loop opens a pull request and stops, and every merge in this repo is deliberate. The authority surfaces it may not touch are an explicit list (aletheia/policy.py, the trust modules, machine_binding, core, supervisor, config/, .claude/, CLAUDE.md, docs/PLAYBOOK.md and more), path-normalized so ./config/fleet.json cannot slip past a prefix check. A proposal is read and written at ONE pinned base_sha, so the tree reviewed is the tree changed. The review runs on a DIFFERENT model from the proposal where one is available, and when it cannot, the PR body says in plain words that the pass was a consistency check and not an independent opinion. project_loop.status reports NEVER_RUN today - EXPERIMENTAL until the first proposed PR is read by the operator. Stranger text is separated from operator intent: an issue body, an issue title, a workflow name and a CI job name are all written by people who are not the operator, and until 2026-09-01 they were concatenated into the OBJECTIVE - the same string the proposer and the reviewer read as their task. They now travel as sanitized `evidence` in a labelled context field, both system prompts say what that field is, and the reviewer is explicitly the injection check. HALT is re-read across every long gap (before the review, before the first write), not once at the top of a cycle that then spends minutes in two model calls.
capabilities.verification: tests/test_code_worker.py: every protected authority surface refused (including path-normalization bypasses), the review asserted to be a second judge, candidates asserted to be read at the exact pinned ref; stranger text never reaches the instruction field, role headers and fenced blocks cannot pose as structure, and halting mid-flight creates nothing on GitHub

capabilities.description: Standing LOCAL permission for the autonomous code loop to open a bounded number of pull requests
capabilities.caller: python -m aletheia.code_trust on|status|off (local PC only); read by aletheia.project_loop and aletheia.code_worker
capabilities.notes: Bounded by a PR ceiling and an expiry, machine-bound since 2026-09-01, and it authorizes PROPOSING only - it confers no merge authority anywhere.
capabilities.verification: tests/test_machine_binding.py: raising max_prs on a real grant breaks the binding rather than raising the ceiling

capabilities.description: Offline local models (Ollama) as a reasoning provider when the subscription clients are unavailable
capabilities.caller: aletheia.reasoner via aletheia.local_model_pool; policy in aletheia.reasoning_gateway; python -m aletheia.local_ai to provision
capabilities.notes: DISABLED by default and reported so by reasoning_gateway.status (enabled=false, source=default). The invariant that matters more than the plumbing: a local model must never become the authority for a critical decision merely because Claude is out. The gateway's policy tiers are what enforce that - critical work degrades honestly instead of silently dropping to a smaller model, and shadow mode exists so a local model can be compared without being trusted. NEEDS_CONFIGURATION until the operator provisions models and opts in.
capabilities.verification: tests/test_local_ai_integration.py: the critical tier never downgrades to a local answer (the local pool is asserted NOT CALLED when the subscriptions are down, so it fails instead of quietly answering); a remote Ollama endpoint is refused; a failed activation leaves local routing disabled

capabilities.description: The operator's ChatGPT subscription used as a reasoning fallback through a real browser session - no API key
capabilities.caller: aletheia.reasoner (fallback after the Claude CLI) and aletheia.perception, both via aletheia.reasoning_gateway; python -m aletheia.chatgpt_session to initialize the profile
capabilities.notes: Gated on an OPERATOR LEASE that unattended contexts must never inherit: EVERY always-on entry point drops the lease from its own environment as its first statement — the Core, the supervisor (which also strips it from every child environment), the project loop and the voice room. The last two matter most and were missed by the first pass: they run as their OWN Windows scheduled tasks, so no parent scrubs anything and Task Scheduler hands them the user's environment. A watchdog, project loop, scheduled process or voice room therefore cannot open a visible ChatGPT window on the operator's screen. chatgpt_session.status reports ready=false ('browser profile has not been initialized') today.
capabilities.verification: tests/test_browser_reasoner_windows_mode.py: the always-on entry points are enumerated from the SCHEDULED TASK REGISTRY, not a hand-written list, and each main() is asserted to drop the lease before it parses an argument — a new always-on task cannot be registered without doing the same

capabilities.description: Answer now, deliver the real answer when it exists: a durable slot for a reply that takes longer than the room can be held open
capabilities.caller: aletheia.core POST /api/voice opens a slot and GET /api/followup polls it; aletheia.presence speaks a READY slot; interface/voice.js collects it
capabilities.notes: Built because the failure was real and reported by the operator: he asked Thea something, got an acknowledgement, and never received the finished answer - the planner takes ten to thirty seconds and the request was being dropped when the room closed. A slot is PENDING, then READY or FAILED; a FAILED slot says so out loud rather than staying silent, because silence is the bug.
capabilities.verification: tests/test_voice.py: an arbitrary ask returns within 2 seconds with a followup_id, and the real sentence is collectable from that slot

capabilities.description: Authorize a GOAL with a budget instead of approving every step of it, and work it until the budget, the deadline or HALT stops it
capabilities.caller: python -m aletheia.mission start|status|stop|kinds (local PC only); aletheia.project_loop.run_mission_slice sweeps every repository against the live mission
capabilities.notes: Built because the operator asked for something the repo could not do: 'look at all my projects and fix the problems'. Nothing here could work on a GOAL - every capability was scoped to one action with one approval, and the code loop did one repair in one repository per run. A mission is not new authority: what it may cover is a POSITIVE allowlist (MISSION_ALLOWED, today just code.autonomous, which has no merge path), and operator_always is refused outright, so spending, sending, booking, phoning, interactive browsing and secret-filling still ask every time inside a mission exactly as outside one. It carries a wall-clock deadline AND a work ceiling and ends itself on whichever comes first; HALT is re-read between every repository; it is machine-bound like every standing grant, so a mission file arriving over git sync is inert. EXPERIMENTAL because no mission has been run on the operator's PC - the first live sweep is what promotes it.
capabilities.verification: tests/test_mission.py: 23 tests - the budget really stops it, a refused review costs nothing, progress survives a restart, a record edited to widen itself or raise its own ceiling is inert, halting mid-sweep stops after one repository, and one bad repository does not end the sweep

capabilities.description: Look into a question and answer it from real sources, with every claim bound to the page it came from
capabilities.caller: voice ('look into X', 'find out about X', 'what do you know about X'); intercom kind 'research' (LOCAL - the browser is on the PC); python -m aletheia.research; aletheia.mission kind 'research'
capabilities.notes: The second mission kind, and the one that gets daily use. It only ever READS - no approval, no interaction, nothing sent, nothing spent - which is why it can sit under a mission budget at all. There is no search API and there will not be one (No6: no API keys), so it searches the way a person does, through the operator's own browser. What separates it from asking a model the same question is that every claim carries the page it came from and a claim citing a page that was not read is DROPPED in code, not discouraged in a prompt - a model that invents a citation is not caught by asking it not to. Bounded to 5 sources, one page per site, and the report says what the sources failed to settle and how many claims were dropped. EXPERIMENTAL until a real question has been answered on the PC.
capabilities.verification: tests/test_research.py: 16 tests - an invented citation is dropped and the drop is said out loud, one page per site, search engines are never cited as sources, a broken search costs the query rather than the question, no sources is an honest refusal rather than an invented answer, HALT stops it before the browser opens, and the module is asserted never to reach browse.interact or any secret

capabilities.description: Take a request in plain English and carry it out step by step without asking again - never spending money
capabilities.caller: python -m aletheia.agenda '<request>'; aletheia.mission kind 'anything' runs it under a budget
capabilities.notes: The operator's ask, in his words: 'take any request I give it and execute it except no spending money'. The pieces existed - the planner compiles plain English into validated commands, the intercom executes one, a mission bounds a budget - but every plan filed an approval and waited, so 'any request' meant 'any request, once you come back and click yes'. THREE refusals, all enforced in code: (1) MONEY names every capability that moves money, refused at compile time and before every step, with no flag that turns it off; (2) approve/deny are refused, because an agenda that can approve things can file the approval for the purchase it is forbidden to make and then grant it - that hole would have converted every other refusal into a speed bump; (3) halt/resume are refused, because a kill switch the agent can lift is decoration. Also refused: intent (recursion), rule (authority outliving the mission) and dispatch (someone else's compute). Drafting mail IS allowed and stays safe because mail.send_approved delivers only drafts he approved - she writes the letter and never posts it. EXPERIMENTAL: no agenda has run on his PC.
capabilities.verification: tests/test_agenda.py: 18 tests - every money capability refused with nothing executed first, approve/deny/halt/resume/intent/rule/dispatch refused while allowed steps in the same plan still run, refusals said out loud rather than swallowed, halting mid-plan stops at the next step, one failing step does not abandon the rest, and the source is asserted to contain no money-override flag

capabilities.description: Create and edit real files - documents, notes, data, captions - inside a workspace she owns, keeping every version she replaces
capabilities.caller: intercom kinds file_write/file_edit/file_read/file_list (LOCAL - the workspace is a directory on his PC), reachable from an agenda; python -m aletheia.workspace
capabilities.notes: She could think but not hand him anything - no document, no spreadsheet, no file - so 'open my resume and fix the formatting' compiled to nothing. Most of what sounds like desktop control is a FILE operation wearing a GUI, and driving Word to edit a document is the dangerous way to do what a text edit does safely. The boundary is what makes it safe: one root (~/Aletheia by default), every path RESOLVED before it is checked so `../` and symlinks out of the workspace fail the same test, absolute paths refused rather than quietly made relative (a confident write to a path nobody named is worse than a refusal - caught by its own boundary test), and a root that resolves to his home or Desktop refused as 'not a workspace, everything under it'. Every overwrite keeps the previous version in .versions/ and `restore` puts one back, so a mistake costs a paragraph rather than an afternoon. Reading is deliberately WIDER than writing - she may read a file he names anywhere, because reading destroys nothing - but writing is workspace-only with no argument that widens it. Text formats only: a binary format she cannot write correctly is a corrupted file with a confident receipt.
capabilities.verification: tests/test_workspace.py: 21 tests - traversal, symlinked files AND symlinked directories, absolute paths, a root that is everything, the version history being uneditable, an edit matching nothing raising rather than passing silently, an ambiguous edit asking for context, restore round-tripping, and no half-written file surviving

capabilities.description: Look at the desktop - what windows are open, what is in them - without touching anything
capabilities.caller: intercom kind 'computer_observe' (LOCAL), reachable from an agenda; aletheia.computer.observe
capabilities.notes: The desktop was entirely unreachable from an agenda: computer.control is operator_always, so the planner could not compile a step that touched it at all. Splitting the action set by EFFECT is what gives her eyes without hands. list_windows and inspect_controls change nothing; clicking, typing, launching and closing windows can destroy an afternoon of somebody's work, so those keep computer.control's hash-bound operator approval and are NOT reachable from an agenda. observe() REFUSES a mutating step rather than filtering it out, because a caller that asked to click and was quietly handed a window list would report success for work that never happened.
capabilities.verification: tests/test_agenda.py: observation is read-tier and agenda-reachable while invoke/set_text/close_window/open_app are asserted absent from OBSERVE_ACTIONS, and a plan mixing the two is refused whole
